questions.stem: In anaemia, what should be ruled out before surgery?
In anaemia with low ferritin and TSAT, when is IV iron (Ferinject) given?
questions.answer: If surgery is 4 wk or less away, moderate anaemia or bleeding, or absorption problems

questions.stem: What are the three parts of patient blood management in anaemia?
questions.answer: Know the allowable blood loss, minimise blood loss, maintain cardiac output

questions.stem: Anaemia in males is defined as Hb less than ____.
Anaemia in females is defined as Hb less than ____.
Anaemia in pregnancy is defined as Hb less than ____.
When should haemoglobin be measured before surgery?
questions.answer: Before all major surgery, and in anyone with significant history, especially cardiovascular or respiratory disease

questions.stem: What history or sign should make you suspect anaemia before surgery?
Which of these is a listed feature of symptomatic anaemia?
What does the anaemia investigation panel include?
questions.answer: Iron studies, B12 and folate, reticulocyte count, creatinine

questions.stem: In anaemia, what should be done with elective surgery where possible?
Which haematinics are used to treat the cause of anaemia?
questions.answer: IV or oral iron, B12 injections, folate

questions.stem: Erythropoietin is useful in which group of anaemic patients?
Why has transfusion in anaemia become more conservative?
questions.answer: Transfusion morbidity, and better tolerance of low Hb than once thought

In iron deficiency anaemia treatment, which rare serious reaction occurs in under 0.1% of patients?

If both B12 and folate are low in megaloblastic anaemia, which should be started first, and why?
questions.answer: Start B12 before folate, to avoid subacute combined degeneration of the cord

questions.stem: In anaemia of renal failure, at what GFR should the patient be referred to nephrology?
In anaemia of renal failure, what is the target haemoglobin?
In anaemia of renal failure, what should be done with erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESA)?
What is the basic defect in thalassaemia?
questions.answer: Absent or reduced synthesis of alpha or beta globin chains

questions.stem: In thalassaemia, which severity is transfusion dependent with serious iron overload?
In thalassaemia history-taking, which cardiac problem should be asked about?
Why may the airway be difficult in a patient with thalassaemia?
questions.answer: Marrow overgrowth deforms the bone and face

questions.answer: Parts of Africa, the Mediterranean, Middle East and India

questions.stem: In sickle cell disease, what do sickled cells do to small vessels?
questions.answer: Block them, causing haemolysis and infarction

questions.stem: Which factors can trigger sickling in sickle cell disease?
questions.answer: Hypoxia, hypothermia or fever, acidosis, hypovolaemia, infection

questions.stem: How predictable is the clinical course of sickle cell disease?

In sickle cell disease, which crisis mainly affects children with sudden splenic pooling of red cells?
In sickle cell disease, what does chronic haemolysis cause?
Which genotypes give a positive sickle screening test?
In sickle cell disease, which cells on the blood film suggest an atrophic spleen?
Supportive care in sickle cell disease includes folic acid, vaccinations and ____.
How is a sickle cell crisis managed?
questions.answer: Rest, IV fluids, antibiotics, oxygen, warming and good analgesia

questions.stem: In sickle cell disease, transfusion aims for HbS of less than ____.
Which sickle cell crises may need transfusion, after discussion with haematology?
Before any operation in sickle cell disease, which specialty should be consulted?
What should be avoided perioperatively in sickle cell disease?
questions.answer: Hypoxia, dehydration, infection, acidosis, hypothermia and pain
